title: Give each order status its own state

task.text: `Order` switches on a status enum in every method.

Refactor to the **State** pattern: each phase of an order becomes an object that decides what every event does. The public behaviour of `Order` must not change, including which events are rejected with `IllegalStateException`.

items: Add `interface OrderState` with `OrderState pay(String)`, `OrderState ship(String)`, `OrderState cancel()`, each returning the next state, and `String describe()`.
Make one class per phase: new, paid, shipped, cancelled. Receipt and tracking live only in the states that have them.
`Order` keeps a single private `OrderState` and forwards events: `state = state.pay(r)`. Keep `new Order()`. The `Status` enum goes away.

checks.title: New, paid, shipped read as before
New and paid orders can be cancelled
Illegal events raise and change nothing
A cancelled order accepts no events
Each phase is its own class

hints.text: Find what varies: what each event does depends on the phase. Give the phase an object of its own, so that `Order` no longer asks which phase it is in.
Declare `OrderState` with a default for every event that rejects it, then let each phase override only the events it allows. An event returns the successor state, which `Order` stores.
